validations: AC-01: validate protected requirement — Given selected source `src/app.py` with protected SHA/content, a typed intent for `src/app.py` produces a canonical `GeneratedSourcePatch` using the exact protected SHA and a strict diff that applies to the protected content.

AC-02: validate protected requirement — Given no selected source entry for `prototypes/fml-data-readiness/index.html`, a non-empty typed intent produces a canonical new-file patch with `EMPTY_SHA256`, `/dev/null` old header and exact target new header. The unchanged P2-V0.23.25 safe engine can validate/apply it when the target truly does not exist.

AC-03: validate protected requirement — The DSPy typed output schema for live implementation generation contains path/content intent and does not require or accept model-supplied `expected_base_sha256` or `unified_diff` fields.

AC-04: validate protected requirement — `ImplementationGeneration.proposal` remains the existing `ImplementationProposal`, and `ProtectedImplementationRuntime` / agentic candidate validation require no alternate mutation path.

AC-05: validate protected requirement — Duplicate target paths and after-content identical to authoritative before-content are rejected as protected output validation failures before candidate admission.

AC-06: validate protected requirement — If a path absent from selected context actually exists in the workspace, the generated empty-base proposal is rejected by the unchanged safe proposal validator. No source mutation occurs.

AC-07: validate protected requirement — Focused fixtures cover ordinary trailing-newline text, text without a trailing newline, empty existing text to non-empty content, and stable identical renderer output. Every supported fixture round-trips through the strict patch engine with exact expected after-content.

AC-08: validate protected requirement — Traversal, absolute paths, secret-sensitive target/content, unsupported extension, binary/NUL content, symlink and hierarchy-conflict cases remain rejected by existing protected boundaries.
AC-09: validate protected requirement — Malformed typed file-intent output is classified `validation_failed`; provider timeout/rate/transport behavior remains separately classified.

AC-10: validate protected requirement — Repair guidance no longer asks models to repair diff mechanics. The existing one final validator repair per work unit, cache-distinct final context token and admitted agent rules remain unchanged.

AC-11: validate protected requirement — Focused tests, full API regression, client checks, protected promotion evaluation, Bounded Autonomy, Workstream Spec Validation and required DSPy compilation/verification pass on the exact reviewed head.

AC-12: validate protected requirement — After merge, the exact application source reaches READY production deployment. `/health` and `/ready` are HTTP 200 with database/providers ready, and required production preflights remain green.

AC-13: validate protected requirement — An authenticated retry of Engineering Run `3a1ba66a-5649-42b6-81ee-91684fe06bbc` or equivalent real work must no longer fail because the model cannot produce mechanically valid unified diffs. Success is progression into BUILD or a later bounded failure whose evidence is unrelated to model-owned diff syntax.
risks: No canonical downstream contracts, no safe engine rejects collisions, no unsafe paths, no unsupported targets, no symlinks, no secrets, no hierarchy conflicts, no other violations.
